cli.usage:
Usage: cohive <command>

  login [--server <url>] [--tools claude-code,codex]
                     Pair this computer: opens the authorization page in your browser; click "Authorize" (the full command with the URL is under "Profile" on the web).
                     Inside a repository where cohive init has run, the server URL and tools are read from the repository config;
                     on an already paired computer, logging in another tool issues a token right away without authorizing again
  login --resume     Pick up a device authorization that was waiting for admin approval
  login --token-stdin --server <url>
                     Fallback: read a token issued by an admin from standard input
  web [--server <url>] [--workspace <name>]
                     Open the Cohive web UI in your browser without a password (uses this computer's pairing; inside a repository, follows its config)
  init [--tools claude-code,codex] [--server <url>] [--workspace <name>]
                     Write Cohive's MCP config, confirmation rules and the /cohive skill into the current project
  status             List the logins saved on this computer (tokens are not shown)
  version            Show the version of cohive on this computer
  mcp-proxy --server <url> --workspace <name> --tool <tool>
                     Local proxy called by coding tools; you do not need to run it yourself
  hook --server <url> --workspace <name> --tool <tool>
                     Called by coding tools' session hooks to add a reminder line when something new concerns you; you do not need to run it yourself.
                     Add --check to find out why no reminder shows up

Credentials are stored in ~/.config/cohive/credentials.json (readable only by you); set COHIVE_CONFIG_DIR to use another directory.
Set COHIVE_LANG (for example en or zh-CN) to change the language of this CLI.
cli.login.token_stdin_empty: no token read: pass the token your admin gave you (it starts with cohive_) on standard input, for example pbpaste | cohive login --server {{.Server}} --token-stdin
cli.status.none: Not logged in yet. Run cohive login --server <Cohive server URL> and authorize in your browser.
cli.status.devices_header: Server	Account	Device ID	Paired at
cli.status.logins_header: Server	Workspace	Account	Tool	Logged in at
